decisions.reason: A polymer concrete drain housing is a core component that fits the firm's integrated drainage families, and its own web page shows visible commitment, so dropping it after one year is unlikely.
Floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's announced direction toward accessible, low-profile systems, so management will keep it and attribute any weak early results to market ramp-up.
The designer shower drain has a dedicated web page and supports the firm's design-quality positioning, so prior investment and public commitment favor keeping it.
A shower element with integrated slope matches the integrated, renovation-friendly strategy, and its development effort encourages persistence despite only a brief mention online.
The backflow-protected basement drain was publicly announced as a specific in-house development with its own page, a strong commitment that management will want to justify.
The air-admittance valve is more peripheral to the shower-drainage focus and was only mentioned online, but as a low-cost complementary sanitary item it is still likely kept.
